sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5062 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioner/A1 seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.229 of 2019 of Ongole I Town Police Station, Prakasam District, which was registered against him for the offences under Sections 420, 188, 273 of IPC and Sec.58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006').

entities.text: Ongole I Town Police Station, Prakasam District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 10.08.2019 at 01.30 p.m., when the complainant along with his staff proceeded to Anjali Cool Drinks and Fancy Shop, Court Centre,
Ongole, they found a person sitting on a motor bike with a bag containing tobacco products, on enquiry, he revealed that he has been purchasing and selling the tobacco products illegally, the Police seized the same under the cover of mediator's report and registered the same as a case in Crime No.229 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.

entities.text:
Anjali Cool Drinks and Fancy Shop, Court Centre,
Ongole
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto filed on the report of the Police Officer of Ongole I Town Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners under Sections Sections 420, 188, 273 of IPC and Sec.58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, are hereby quashed.
